target_paper_title: IA-GGAD: Zero-shot Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection via Invariant and Affinity Learning

gold_annotations.topic: This paper studies zero-shot generalist graph anomaly detection, where a single model is trained on multiple source-domain graphs and then applied to unseen target graphs without target-domain retraining or fine-tuning. The task focuses on node-level anomaly detection across diverse graph domains such as citation, social, e-commerce, and financial networks, under substantial cross-domain variation in node features and graph structure.
gold_annotations.golden_gap: The paper argues that prior graph anomaly detection methods are largely built for a single graph and must be retrained for each new dataset, which makes them unsuitable for one-model-for-all deployment. Even recent generalist or cross-domain methods do not fully resolve the fundamental domain shifts in this setting: Feature Space Shift, where node features differ in scale, dimensionality, or semantics across domains, and Graph Structure Shift, where connectivity patterns differ so that normal structure in one graph may look anomalous in another. The paper further states that ARC still needs a few target-domain normal examples at inference and that UNPrompt depends on consistent attribute semantics and single-source training, leaving a gap for a truly zero-shot method that can handle both feature and structural shifts together.
gold_annotations.golden_method: The proposed method is IA-GGAD, an end-to-end framework that combines invariant learning for feature shift and affinity learning for structure shift. It first aligns raw node attributes into a shared latent space, then builds a shared invariant feature pool of domain-invariant prototypes using a modified VQ-VAE-style module. These prototypes are fused with multi-hop GCN embeddings to produce graph-invariant node representations, and residual differences across GNN layers are used to capture anomaly-relevant semantic deviations. To address graph structure shift, the method adds a graph affinity encoder that learns local homophily-based affinity scores in an unsupervised way. At inference time, IA-GGAD combines a residual dispersion score with a structure-sensitive local affinity score through weighted fusion to produce a final anomaly score for nodes on unseen graphs.
gold_annotations.gold_experiment: The paper evaluates IA-GGAD in a pretrain-only zero-shot setting using source graphs PubMed, Flickr, Questions, and YelpChi, and testing on unseen target graphs ACM, Facebook, Amazon, Cora, CiteSeer, BlogCatalog, Reddit, and Weibo. It compares against sixteen strong baselines spanning supervised GNNs, semi-supervised GAD, unsupervised GAD, and the two state-of-the-art generalist methods ARC and UNPrompt. Performance is reported with AUROC and AUPRC averaged over five random seeds. The study includes main comparisons, ablations that remove the invariant or affinity components, sensitivity analysis for the fusion weight, and an analysis relating results to measured Feature Space Shift and Graph Structure Shift. The paper also reports scalability experiments on large financial graphs including DGraph, T-Finance, and Elliptic.
